chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who broke the eggs of pigeons, and in the eggs were chicks that had moved. He (peace be upon him) said: He must give charity for every chick that had moved inside it by sacrificing a sheep, and give charity with its meat if he is in ihram. And if the chicks had not moved, he must give charity for their value in silver, and buy with it fodder and throw it for the pigeons of the Sanctuary.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for breaking pigeon eggs while in ihram?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar highlights the juristic distinction between 'movement' (harakah) as the threshold for full animal sacrifice versus monetary compensation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise biological indicators in ritual law. It specifically addresses the scenario of a pilgrim in ihram breaking pigeon eggs in the Haram, linking the compensation to the sanctity of the sacred precinct by directing the monetary value toward fodder for the Haram's pigeons. This demonstrates the practical application of kaffarah in maintaining the ecological and ritual integrity of the holy sites.
